paper.title_en: Imprints of Modified Gravity on the Stability of Hybrid Stars
paper.abstract_en: The present study investigates static anisotropic hybrid-star configurations containing hadronic matter and strange quark matter in the framework of $f(\mathbb {Q},\mathcal {T})$ gravity, where $\mathbb {Q}$ is the non-metricity scalar and $\mathcal {T}$ denotes the trace of the energy-momentum tensor. The Finch-Skea spacetime geometry is adopted to construct exact solutions of the modified field equations. The physical viability of the resulting stellar model is examined through a detailed graphical analysis of the metric potentials, matter variables, radial and tangential pressures, anisotropic contribution, radial gradients, quark-sector density and pressure components, equation of state parameter, mass profile, and energy conditions. In addition, the stability of the configuration is tested by considering the compactness factor, gravitational redshift, sound-speed constraints, Herrera cracking condition, and adiabatic index. The analysis is carried out for the compact object EXO 1785-248, whose observed mass and radius are taken as $1.3^{+0.2}_{-0.2}M_\odot $ and $8.849^{+0.4}_{-0.4}\,\textrm{km}$, respectively. The obtained results indicate that the considered $f(\mathbb {Q},\mathcal {T})$ model can provide a consistent theoretical setting for describing the internal structure and stability behavior of hybrid stars.
